SMTO-EXE-0265 — This workflow was changed since you opened it

GUID: 7f946b75-870d-5af1-9bc6-4e46221508d2
Slug: recipe-revision-mismatch
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: recipes

What happened

  • A newer version of this workflow was saved, for example from another window, or the version this run expected is gone. SMTO stopped so it doesn't overwrite the newer version or run an outdated one.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you were editing, copy any text you changed, then select Cancel. Reloading drops unsaved edits, so keep a copy first.
  2. Reload the Workflows page and open the workflow with Edit to see the latest version. You'll then be working on the newest saved version.
  3. Make your change again and select Save changes, or select Run now to run the latest version. The save or run now matches the version SMTO has stored.
  4. If a run stopped partway with this message, open it from History with Open run and check which steps already finished before running again. A new run starts from the beginning and could repeat changes.

What success looks like

  • Save changes succeeds, or Run now starts a new run that shows in the workflow's History.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the workflow's name, to the person who manages SMTO. Close other windows or tabs that have this workflow open so they don't keep saving over each other.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The workflow revision check failed: the edit's expected revision is out of date, the pinned or scheduled revision is missing or differs from the current definition, or a resumed task's stored workflow differs from the one being loaded.

What this means

  • A pinned recipe revision is missing or differs from the current definition, an expected revision conflicts, or resumed workflow content differs from its durable checkpoint. Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.

Why this can happen

  • A pinned recipe revision is missing or differs from the current definition, an expected revision conflicts, or resumed workflow content differs from its durable checkpoint.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare recipe revision, expected_revision and the durable run's pinned artifact; retain the original run's evidence.

How to fix it

  • Compare expected_revision or agent_recipe_revision with the recipe's current recipe_revision, and confirm the pinned revision exists (recipes route update_agent_recipe, store.create_run, apply_recipe_update, native_flow, scheduling.scope, runtime.initialize). Reload the current definition for new work; a resumed run must keep its original pinned definition.
  • Reload and review the current workflow for new work; resolve the original pinned definition before resuming an existing run.

Retry and execution caution

  • Review the workflow and its current run evidence before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • A reviewed new invocation uses the intended revision, while resumed work retains its original pinned definition.

What not to do

  • Never repeat a write whose effect remains unknown.

Technical notes

  • Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
